# konnect_ai_cost_budget (Resource)

AICostBudget Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "konnect_ai_cost_budget" "my_aicostbudget" {
  exempt = {
    labels = {
      key = "value"
    }
    name     = "...my_name..."
    priority = 100
    scope = {
      each    = "...my_each..."
      filters = "{ \"see\": \"documentation\" }"
    }
    validity = {
      from  = "...my_from..."
      until = "...my_until..."
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `exempt` (Attributes) The body of a request that creates or replaces an exemption. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--exempt))
- `limit` (Attributes) The body of a request that creates or replaces a limit budget. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limit))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity creation date.
- `created_by` (String) The `id` of the user or system account that created the budget, which the server records. A person with a budget of their own can replace and delete only the budgets they created.

`null` for a budget created before the service recorded creators.
- `id` (String) Contains a unique identifier used for this resource.
- `name` (String) A human-readable name for the budget, unique within the organization.
- `posture` (String) What the budget declares should happen when spend reaches the limit. Nothing enforces it.
- `priority` (Number) The budget's priority, from 1, the highest, to 100, the lowest. The budget list can filter and sort by it, but balances and notification rules don't use it.
- `updated_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity update date.

### Nested Schema for `exempt`

Optional:

- `labels` (Map of String) Key-value metadata on the budget. The budget list can filter by label. Balances and notification rules ignore labels.
- `name` (String) A human-readable name for the budget, unique within the organization.

1 to 255 characters.
Not Null
- `priority` (Number) The budget's priority, from 1, the highest, to 100, the lowest. The budget list can filter and sort by it, but balances and notification rules don't use it.

Defaults to `100`.
Default: 100
- `scope` (Attributes) The usage the exemption covers.

A replacement can't change it and must repeat it exactly: reordered filters or values count as a change.

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity creation date.
- `created_by` (String) The `id` of the user or system account that created the budget, which the server records. A person with a budget of their own can replace and delete only the budgets they created.

`null` for a budget created before the service recorded creators.

<a id="nestedatt--exempt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `exempt.scope`

Optional:

- `each` (String) The field that splits the budget. With `each`, the limit applies separately to every value of that field, such as each subject. Each value gets its own derived budget, and usage without a value for the field belongs to none of them.

A fixed usage field or `tags.<key>`, or `null` for a pooled budget, whose limit applies to all its usage together. An exemption can't use `each`. If the filters rule out every value of the field, or every branch fixes it to the same value with `eq`, the request fails with `400`, because the budget would have nothing to split. Defaults to `null`.
- `filters` (String) The filters that select the usage the budget counts. Usage must match every filter. An empty list covers all of the organization's usage.

At most 15 predicates in total across all groups, each inside at most 4 nested groups.
Not Null; Parsed as JSON.


<a id="nestedatt--exempt--validity"></a>
### Nested Schema for `exempt.validity`

Optional:

- `from` (String) When the exemption starts, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or as a date-time with a UTC offset and an IANA time zone in brackets, such as `2026-08-16T00:00:00+02:00[Europe/Budapest]`.

The service converts an RFC 3339 timestamp to UTC and keeps a date-time's IANA time zone. Defaults to the budget's `created_at`, also when a replacement omits it.
- `until` (String) When the exemption ends, in the same formats as `from`, which the service normalizes the same way.

Must be later than `from`.
Not Null

Optional:

- `labels` (Map of String) Key-value metadata on the budget. The budget list can filter by label. Balances and notification rules ignore labels.
- `limit` (Attributes) The spending limit for each budget window. With `each`, every derived budget gets this limit. Not Null (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limit--limit))
- `name` (String) A human-readable name for the budget, unique within the organization.

1 to 255 characters.
Not Null
- `posture` (String) What the budget declares should happen when spend reaches the limit. Nothing enforces it.

Defaults to `advisory`.
possible known values include one of ["advisory", "enforce"]; Default: "advisory"
- `priority` (Number) The budget's priority, from 1, the highest, to 100, the lowest. The budget list can filter and sort by it, but balances and notification rules don't use it.

Defaults to `100`.
Default: 100
- `scope` (Attributes) The usage the budget covers.

A replacement can't change it and must repeat it exactly: reordered filters or values count as a change.
Not Null; Requires replacement if changed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limit--scope))
- `window` (Attributes) The budget window: the period the limit applies to, such as a calendar month. When one window ends, the next starts.

A replacement can't change it.
Not Null; Requires replacement if changed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limit--window))

- `created_by` (String) The `id` of the user or system account that created the budget, which the server records. A person with a budget of their own can replace and delete only the budgets they created.

`null` for a budget created before the service recorded creators.

<a id="nestedatt--limit--limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limit.limit`

Optional:

- `currency` (String) The currency of `value`. Not Null; must be "USD"
- `value` (String) The amount of the limit in major units of `currency`, as a decimal string such as `5000` or `0.2`.

At most 9 fractional digits, with no sign, exponent, or leading zeros. The service removes trailing fractional zeros, so `12.50` is stored and returned as `12.5`.
Not Null


<a id="nestedatt--limit--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limit.scope`

Optional:

- `each` (String) The field that splits the budget. With `each`, the limit applies separately to every value of that field, such as each subject. Each value gets its own derived budget, and usage without a value for the field belongs to none of them.

A fixed usage field or `tags.<key>`, or `null` for a pooled budget, whose limit applies to all its usage together. An exemption can't use `each`. If the filters rule out every value of the field, or every branch fixes it to the same value with `eq`, the request fails with `400`, because the budget would have nothing to split. Defaults to `null`.
- `filters` (String) The filters that select the usage the budget counts. Usage must match every filter. An empty list covers all of the organization's usage.

At most 15 predicates in total across all groups, each inside at most 4 nested groups.
Not Null; Parsed as JSON.


<a id="nestedatt--limit--window"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limit.window`

Optional:

- `anchor` (String) A time when a budget window starts. Windows start a whole number of intervals before or after it. The intervals count in the local time of the anchor's time zone, so calendar units such as months stay aligned to the calendar. A window that would start on a day its month doesn't have, such as the 31st, starts on the month's last day.

A date-time with a UTC offset and an IANA time zone in brackets, such as `2026-01-01T00:00:00+01:00[Europe/Budapest]`, in a year from 1970 to 2200.
Not Null
- `interval` (String) The length of each budget window, as an ISO 8601 duration such as `P1M` for a month or `P1D` for a day.

From 1 second to 100 years, in whole milliseconds.
Not Null

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = konnect_ai_cost_budget.my_konnect_ai_cost_budget
  id = "5f9fd312-a987-4628-b4c5-bb4f4fddd5f7"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import konnect_ai_cost_budget.my_konnect_ai_cost_budget "5f9fd312-a987-4628-b4c5-bb4f4fddd5f7"
```
